jei.kiloton.info.ore: Uranium ore (pitchblende) lies deep in stone and deepslate, from Y -56 to 40, about as common as gold. An iron pickaxe gets raw uranium out of it, and a Geiger counter crackles near it.
jei.kiloton.info.core: Goes into the pit of a Nuclear Bomb, up to six cores. Uranium counts 4 kg each against a critical mass of 12 kg, plutonium 2 kg against 4 kg. Below one critical mass only the explosive lenses go off.
jei.kiloton.info.tamper: A shell of depleted uranium around the pit: it cuts the critical masses by a third and adds fast fissions (+20%% yield).
jei.kiloton.info.bomb: Two blocks long. Load the pit from its panel, set the countdown, lift the safety cover and press the red button. A redstone signal or a Remote Detonator arms it too.
jei.kiloton.info.detonator: Sneak-use it on a Nuclear Bomb to link it. Use it anywhere to open the keypad: the bomb's six-digit arming code (on its panel) arms or disarms it by radio, up to 10 km away by default.
jei.kiloton.info.geiger: Held in either hand it clicks with the dose rate: the natural background (about 12 µR/h), uranium ore and nuclear materials nearby, fallout after a blast. Use it to read the dose you have absorbed.

item.kiloton.shelter_meter.desc: Use it inside a room: is it closed, what blast do its walls hold, how much fallout do they stop, is the air filtered.
item.kiloton.rocket_motor.desc: Solid-fuel motor for a ballistic missile.
item.kiloton.guidance_unit.desc: Gyroscopes and a flight computer: they take a missile to its target.
item.kiloton.missile.desc: Goes on a Launch Pad. Its warhead is loaded there like a bomb's pit.
kiloton.shelter.open: Not closed: outside air gets in near %s %s %s. A shelter counts only when it is closed on every side, doors shut.
kiloton.shelter.too_big: Not closed: the air space here is larger than %s m³ (open to the outside, or a cave).
kiloton.shelter.walls: The blast wave gets in only above %s psi outside. The first block it would break is %s at %s %s %s (%s block(s) thick).
kiloton.shelter.way_in: It would come from the open air near %s %s %s and reach that block along the air (a passage or a cave); every door and wall on the way adds to the rating.
kiloton.shelter.walls_deep: No way in for the blast wave: rock all round. Only the crater or the fireball can break it.
kiloton.shelter.survives: Survives a %s burst from %s away, %s from %s.
kiloton.shelter.protection: Fallout: the walls cut the gamma %s times.
kiloton.shelter.filtered: Air: clean, filtered by the Air Filter at %s %s %s.
kiloton.shelter.filter_off: Air: the Air Filter at %s %s %s has no power. Fallout dust will seep in.
kiloton.shelter.unfiltered: Air: not filtered. In fallout the dust seeps in over a few minutes; an Air Filter keeps it out.
gui.kiloton.launch.tip.sky: No open sky: at most one light block above (wood, glass)
gui.kiloton.launch.tip.target: Type the target's X and Z, then SET (or Enter). The missile comes down on the ground there.
gui.kiloton.launch.tip.button: Launch: ten seconds of countdown, then the missile lifts off. ABORT stops it until then.
gui.kiloton.launch.tip.missile: A Ballistic Missile (three blocks tall on the pad) or an Intercontinental one (four, with a two-stage warhead)
gui.kiloton.radar.tip: North is up. Red: coming down inside the range (its impact point is the cross). Blue: your own. Recent detonations are rings. Amber circles: devices counting down on the ground (probable bombs).
jei.kiloton.info.solar_panel: Up to 15 FE/t at noon under a clear sky, less in the morning, the evening and the rain, nothing at night or under a roof. Pushes the power down and sideways.
jei.kiloton.info.rtg: Holds one Nuclear Cell and pushes its 40 FE/t out on every side: power with no sun and no fuel, for a bunker's filter or a radar. Sneak-use with an empty hand to take the cell out.
jei.kiloton.info.nuclear_cell: 40 FE/t for two hours of play in an RTG or in any machine's fuel slot. It ages whether the power is used or not, like any radioactive source, and ends as depleted uranium.
jei.kiloton.info.air_filter: Place it in a wall of a closed shelter, fan inside. With 30 FE/t it keeps the fallout dust out of the air; without it the dust seeps in within minutes.
jei.kiloton.info.shelter_meter: Use it in a room to learn if it is closed (and where air gets in), the overpressure it holds and the way the blast wave would take to get in (every wall and door on it), how far from a 20 kt and a 115 kt burst it survives, how much fallout gamma its walls stop and whether its air is filtered.
jei.kiloton.info.radar: A 3x3 base with a rotating antenna on top (it needs a clear circle 5 blocks wide and 3 high above the base). It needs the open sky (only glass over the antenna) and it does not see what hills or buildings round it hide. While powered (40 FE/t, through any block of the base) it tracks every missile in flight within 10 km, and every block of it gives a redstone signal while one is coming down inside that range. Link Radar Displays to it to watch it from a bunker. It also shows every armed device counting down on the ground inside its range as a probable bomb (no alarm, no redstone).
jei.kiloton.info.launch_pad: Put a Ballistic Missile in its slot (it stands on the pad), load the warhead like a bomb's pit, type the target, charge 100k FE, lift the cover and press the switch. Range up to 20 km.
jei.kiloton.info.missile: Flies from its Launch Pad to the ground at the target: a slow vertical liftoff, the arc, a steep dive. 12 s plus a second every 160 m of range.

tooltip.kiloton.nuclear_bomb.info:
An implosion device, two blocks long. Open it to load up to six uranium or plutonium cores into its pit, and a depleted uranium tamper around them: the yield comes from how far past critical the pit is (3 plutonium cores and a tamper make about 20 kt, Fat Man; 6 uranium cores and a tamper about 115 kt).
Set the countdown, lift the safety cover and press the red button, or give it a redstone signal. Everyone within reach is warned. Its panel shows the six-digit code for a Remote Detonator. An armed bomb cannot be broken: disarm it first.
tooltip.kiloton.trinitite.info: Green glass: the ground at the bottom of the crater, melted by the fireball and frozen. Faintly radioactive.
tooltip.kiloton.fallout_dust.info: Radioactive dust that settles downwind of a blast. It is deadly for the first minutes and loses most of its strength over an in-game day (the 7-10 rule). Clear it with a shovel, or stay in a shelter until it decays.
tooltip.kiloton.irradiated_leaves.info: Foliage killed by radiation, as in the Red Forest at Chernobyl: it turns red-brown a day after the dose. It drops nothing.
tooltip.kiloton.geiger_counter.info:
Hold it to hear it click and see its dial, from the natural background (about 12 µR/h) up to 1000 R/h. It hears uranium ore, nuclear materials in your pockets, running reactors and generators, and fallout.
Use it to read the dose you have absorbed (rem): above 100 rem radiation sickness begins.
tooltip.kiloton.uranium_ore.info: Pitchblende, deep in stone, about as common as gold. Mine it with an iron pickaxe or better; it drops raw uranium (Fortune works, Silk Touch keeps the ore).
tooltip.kiloton.deepslate_uranium_ore.in: Pitchblende in deepslate. Mine it with an iron pickaxe or better; it drops raw uranium (Fortune works, Silk Touch keeps the ore).
tooltip.kiloton.uranium_mill.info: Grinds raw uranium (or the ore, from any mod) into yellowcake. Runs on Forge Energy: burn coal in its fuel slot, put a Nuclear Cell there, connect a cable, or place it next to a running Breeder Reactor. Hoppers and pipes work.
tooltip.kiloton.gas_centrifuge.info:
Enriches uranium one step at a time: yellowcake to 4% (reactor fuel), then 20%, then 90% (weapons grade), with depleted uranium left over at every pass. Centrifuges side by side form a cascade and run faster.
Enrichment is hungry, as in reality: a pass takes 3.3 to 5.8 million FE (8,000 to 14,000 FE/t), a uranium core about 139 million. One Breeder Reactor runs about two centrifuges. Runs on Forge Energy.
tooltip.kiloton.breeder_reactor.info: Burns low-enriched uranium and turns depleted uranium into plutonium-239, one for each fuel element. While it runs it makes 30,000 FE/t (600 MW, like the BN-600 fast breeder) and pushes it into the machines and cables next to it.
tooltip.kiloton.core_foundry.info: Casts the pieces of a bomb's pit: four weapons-grade uranium make a uranium core, two plutonium a plutonium core, four depleted uranium a tamper. Runs on Forge Energy.
tooltip.kiloton.raw_uranium.info: Pitchblende straight from the ore. Grind it into yellowcake in a Uranium Mill.
tooltip.kiloton.yellowcake.info: Uranium oxide with natural uranium's 0.7% of U-235. Enrich it in a Gas Centrifuge.
tooltip.kiloton.low_enriched_uranium.inf: 4% U-235: fuel for the Breeder Reactor, or enrich it further in a Gas Centrifuge.
20% U-235. One more pass through a Gas Centrifuge makes it weapons grade.
tooltip.kiloton.weapons_grade_uranium.in: 90% U-235. Four of them make a uranium core in the Core Foundry.
tooltip.kiloton.depleted_uranium.info: Mostly U-238, left over from enrichment. A Breeder Reactor turns it into plutonium; four make a tamper in the Core Foundry.
tooltip.kiloton.plutonium.info: Plutonium-239, bred in a Breeder Reactor. Two make a plutonium core; it also goes into Nuclear Cells.
tooltip.kiloton.uranium_core.info: 4 kg of weapons-grade uranium for a bomb's or a missile's pit. Imploded, uranium goes critical at about 12 kg: you need three cores, more with no tamper.
tooltip.kiloton.plutonium_core.info: 2 kg of plutonium for a bomb's or a missile's pit. Imploded, plutonium goes critical at about 4 kg: two cores with a tamper start a chain reaction, three make a Fat Man.
tooltip.kiloton.uranium_tamper.info: A shell of depleted uranium around the pit: it reflects neutrons, cuts the critical mass by a third and adds a fifth to the yield.
tooltip.kiloton.detonator.info: Sneak-use it on a nuclear bomb to link it. Then use it anywhere in the same dimension, up to 10 km away: type the bomb's six-digit code (shown on its panel) and press ARM or SAFE. Three wrong codes lock the radio for a minute.
tooltip.kiloton.solar_panel.info: Makes up to 15 FE/t at noon under a clear sky, less in the morning, the evening and the rain, nothing at night or under a roof. Power for the early game; machines and cables next to it take it.
tooltip.kiloton.rtg.info: A radioisotope generator. Use it with a Nuclear Cell in hand to put the cell in: it gives 40 FE/t for two hours of play, to cables and machines around it. The cell ages whether the power is used or not. Sneak-use it with an empty hand to take the cell out.
tooltip.kiloton.air_filter.info: Keeps fallout out of a closed shelter. Place it inside the room, its front facing the room: it finds the shelter by itself (up to 4096 blocks of air). Uses 30 FE/t. Without it, fallout dust seeps into a sealed room within a few minutes.
tooltip.kiloton.radar.info:
An early-warning radar, a 3x3 base with a rotating antenna on top (it needs a clear circle 5 blocks wide and 3 high above the base). It needs the open sky (only glass over the antenna) and it does not see what hills or buildings round it hide. Uses 40 FE/t, through any block of the base.
It tracks every missile in flight within 10 km. Use it to open its scope. While a missile it can see is coming down inside its range, every block of it gives a redstone signal: wire it to doors, lamps or alarms. Armed devices counting down inside its range show as probable bombs.
tooltip.kiloton.radar_display.info:
A screen that shows a radar's scope. Sneak-use a radar with it to link it (the whole stack), then place it anywhere in the same dimension, a bunker for instance. Placed with no link, it finds the nearest radar within 128 blocks.
Displays side by side facing the same way join into one big screen, up to 8 by 6; a wide one shows the list of tracks next to the scope. Use a display to open the radar's console.
tooltip.kiloton.launch_pad.info:
Launches ballistic missiles. Put a Ballistic Missile in it and it stands on the pad (it needs 3 blocks of room above). Above that it needs the open sky, or at most one light block (wood, glass, leaves) that the missile breaks on its way out. Load the warhead's pit like a bomb's, type the target's X and Z, charge the pad (a launch takes 100,000 FE), lift the cover and press the switch.
After a 10-second countdown, which you can abort, the missile flies to the target, from 200 m up to 20 km away.
tooltip.kiloton.nuclear_cell.info: A plutonium heat source with thermocouples: 40 FE/t for two hours of play, in a Radioisotope Generator or in any Kiloton machine's fuel slot. When it is spent, what is left is depleted uranium. A Geiger counter hears it.
tooltip.kiloton.shelter_meter.info: Use it inside a room. It tells you whether the room is closed (and where the air gets in), how much overpressure it holds and the way the blast wave would get in (the first wall it breaks, then the others), how close to a Fat Man and to a 115 kt bomb it survives, how much it cuts the radiation, and whether its air is filtered.
tooltip.kiloton.rocket_motor.info: The solid-fuel motor of a ballistic missile. Crafted with a guidance unit and iron blocks into a missile.
tooltip.kiloton.guidance_unit.info: Gyroscopes and a flight computer that take a missile to its target. Crafted with a rocket motor and iron blocks into a missile.
tooltip.kiloton.missile.info: Goes on a Launch Pad, where it stands three blocks tall and its warhead is loaded like a bomb's pit. A missile with no cores still lands with its explosive lenses.
jei.kiloton.info.radar_display: Shows a radar's scope. Sneak-use a radar with it to link it, then place it anywhere in the same dimension; placed with no link it finds the nearest radar within 128 blocks. Displays side by side facing the same way join into one screen, up to 8 by 6.

gui.kiloton.sam.state.6: SAFE: REDSTONE OR KEY TO ARM
gui.kiloton.sam.tip.arm.0: Safe: the launcher rests and it does not fire
gui.kiloton.sam.tip.arm.1: On: switched on by a launch key
gui.kiloton.sam.tip.arm.2: On: switched on by a redstone signal
gui.kiloton.sam.tip.arm.3: On: a launch key and a redstone signal
gui.kiloton.sam.tip.arm: A redstone signal into any block of its deck, or a launch key linked to it, switches it on
gui.kiloton.detector.none2: It lists every detonation in this dimension from now on
gui.kiloton.detector.tip: OPT: optical (bhangmeter), burst in sight, about 15% error. SEIS: seismic, farther away, larger error and a little late.
advancements.kiloton.intercept.title: Hit a Bullet with a Bullet
advancements.kiloton.intercept.descripti: Destroy an incoming missile with an interceptor
tooltip.kiloton.launch_console.info:
Fires up to 8 launch pads together or one after the other. Before placing it, sneak-use it on each launch pad to link it (again to unlink); it keeps its links when you pick it up.
Only pads that are armed (ARM switch on their panel) and ready fire, each at its own target. Press the red button under the cover, or give it a redstone signal. In two-key mode only two launch keys turned by two players fire it.
tooltip.kiloton.launch_key.info:
The two-man rule of real launch control centres: two keys, too far apart for one person to turn both, must be turned within 1.5 s.
Sneak-use the key on a launch console to link it, then place it on a wall within 128 blocks of the console, at least 4 blocks from the other key. Switch the console to two-key mode on its panel.
Linked to an interceptor battery instead (sneak-use it on the battery, place it within 128 blocks), it is the battery's on/off switch: turned, the battery is on.
tooltip.kiloton.air_raid_siren.info:
A dual-tone rotary siren (two rotors, 10 and 12 ports, about 470 and 560 Hz). It sounds while it gets a redstone signal, or while the radar it is linked to tracks a missile coming down inside its range: sneak-use it on a radar before placing it.
It spins up, wails (the motor switched on and off) and winds down. Its sound travels at 343 m/s, so far away it starts late; it carries about a mile.
tooltip.kiloton.sam_launcher.info:
Shoots down missiles. A 3 by 3 deck with a launcher that trains and rises: it needs room, and two blocks of air above. Over that, open sky, or at most one light block that the first interceptor breaks. Sneak-use it on a radar to link it, place it, load interceptors on its four rails and give it power (50,000 FE a shot).
It fires only when switched on: by a redstone signal into any block of its deck, or by a launch key linked to it. Switched on, it keeps its area loaded, so it stands watch with nobody near. When the radar tracks a missile that will pass within its range it predicts where they meet, turns the launcher that way and fires two interceptors, each with a 60% chance to kill. A destroyed missile does not explode: a warhead is built so that only a perfect implosion sets it off. It falls, and its explosive can scatter a little plutonium where it lands. With the IFF switch on its panel turned on it spares the missiles of whoever placed it and of their team; off (the default) it fires at every missile.
tooltip.kiloton.interceptor.info: A small, fast missile with a fragmentation warhead and its own guidance. It goes on the rails of an interceptor battery.
tooltip.kiloton.burst_detector.info:
Logs every nuclear detonation in its dimension after you place it: day and time, distance, direction and the yield it estimates, with its error. It gives a short redstone pulse each time.
Within 3 km it times the double flash of the fireball, like the bhangmeters on the Vela satellites (about 15% error). Farther away it only feels the ground wave, as a seismic station does: the error grows with distance and the wave arrives late, at about 6 km/s.
tooltip.kiloton.potassium_iodide.info:
Stable iodine for the thyroid. One dose saturates it for about a day, so it takes up almost none of the radioactive iodine breathed in with fresh fallout (more than 90% blocked if taken before or soon after).
It does nothing against the gamma rays from the ground, the dust on your skin or any other isotope: it cuts only the part of the dose you breathe in. Iodine was discovered in seaweed ash.
tooltip.kiloton.hazmat_mask.info:
Full-face mask with a filter cartridge: it keeps fallout dust out of your lungs (protection factor 50). Breathing fallout uses the filter up in about half an hour; charcoal in an anvil renews it.
Like the rest of the suit it does not stop gamma rays.
tooltip.kiloton.hazmat_suit.info:
Rubberised coverall. The full suit keeps 95% of the fallout off your body and stops part of the beta from what lands on it.
It does not stop gamma rays: a hazmat suit is not a shelter.
tooltip.kiloton.hazmat_trousers.info: Part of the hazmat suit: it keeps fallout dust off your skin. It does not stop gamma rays.
tooltip.kiloton.hazmat_boots.info: Part of the hazmat suit: it keeps fallout dust off your skin. It does not stop gamma rays.
tooltip.kiloton.decon_shower.info:
Hang it under a ceiling, put a water source next to it, above it or on top of the ceiling block, and turn it on (use it, or with redstone).
Fallout that settled on you keeps irradiating you, indoors too, until you wash it off: half a minute under the shower takes off nearly all of it. Rain and swimming take off only the loose part. A Geiger counter shows what you are carrying.
tooltip.kiloton.warhead_debris.info: Fragments of a warhead broken open by its own explosive, with plutonium smeared on them. A Geiger counter picks them up a few blocks away. Pick them up to clean the place, and wash afterwards.
item.kiloton.raw_lithium.desc: Spodumene. The Uranium Mill turns it into lithium.
item.kiloton.lithium.desc: Natural lithium: 7.5% lithium-6. The exchange column separates it.
item.kiloton.lithium_6.desc: Enriched lithium: struck by a neutron it becomes tritium.
item.kiloton.heavy_water.desc: Water whose hydrogen is deuterium: one part in 6,400 of any water.
item.kiloton.lithium_deuteride.desc: Fusion fuel: 50 kg. Burnt half way, 1.25 megatons.
item.kiloton.icbm.desc: Goes on a Launch Pad. Carries a two-stage warhead three times as far.
gui.kiloton.hbomb.tip.fuel: Fusion fuel: a Lithium-6 Deuteride Charge. Each needs about 15 kt of primary to burn fully.
gui.kiloton.hbomb.tip.spark: Spark plug: a uranium or plutonium core down the axis, which lights the fuel from the inside
gui.kiloton.hbomb.tip.jacket: Jacket: a depleted uranium tamper round the fuel. Doubles the yield, and makes most of the fallout (optional)
gui.kiloton.hbomb.tip.compression: Primary %s of the %s this much fuel needs: %s%% of the fuel burns
advancements.kiloton.lithium.title: The Lightest Metal
advancements.kiloton.fusion_fuel.title: Dry Fuel
advancements.kiloton.thermonuclear.title: The Super
advancements.kiloton.thermonuclear.descr: Light a fusion stage with a fission bomb
tooltip.kiloton.thermonuclear_bomb.info:
A two-stage (Teller-Ulam) device, two blocks long. The primary is a fission bomb: load its pit and tamper as usual. Its X-rays implode the secondary: up to six Lithium-6 Deuteride Charges round a spark plug (a uranium or plutonium core), inside an optional jacket (a Depleted Uranium Tamper).
Each charge is 50 kg of fuel: 1.25 megatons when it burns well, and as much again from the jacket, which the fusion neutrons fission (that is also where most of the fallout comes from: without the jacket the bomb is far cleaner). The more fuel, the stronger the primary it takes: about 15 kt for each charge. Under 3 kt the secondary does not light at all, and without a spark plug most of the fuel is wasted.
Six charges, spark plug and jacket behind a full uranium primary: 15 megatons, Castle Bravo. Timer, arming button, redstone and Remote Detonator work as on the Nuclear Bomb.
tooltip.kiloton.lithium_ore.info: Spodumene, the hard-rock ore of lithium: from Y -16 up into the mountains. Mine it with an iron pickaxe or better; it drops raw lithium (Fortune works, Silk Touch keeps the ore).
tooltip.kiloton.deepslate_lithium_ore.in: Spodumene in deepslate. Mine it with an iron pickaxe or better; it drops raw lithium (Fortune works, Silk Touch keeps the ore).
tooltip.kiloton.raw_lithium.info: Spodumene crystals. The Uranium Mill grinds and roasts them into lithium, two for each piece (four from the ore block).
tooltip.kiloton.lithium.info: Natural lithium is 92.5% lithium-7 and 7.5% lithium-6; a thermonuclear weapon wants the lithium-6. The Isotope Exchange Column separates it: eight lithium in, one lithium-6 out.
tooltip.kiloton.lithium_6.info: Lithium enriched in its light isotope. In the bomb a neutron splits it into helium and tritium on the spot, and the tritium fuses with deuterium: that is why the fuel can be a dry, storable salt instead of liquid hydrogen. Five of these and four Heavy Water make a Lithium-6 Deuteride Charge.
tooltip.kiloton.heavy_water.info: Deuterium oxide. One water molecule in 6,400 carries deuterium; the Isotope Exchange Column draws it out of a bucket of water (and gives the bucket back), at a real cost in energy: 1.8 million FE a flask. Four of these and five Lithium-6 make a Lithium-6 Deuteride Charge.
tooltip.kiloton.lithium_deuteride.info: The fuel of the hydrogen bomb: 50 kg of lithium-6 deuteride pressed into a ring, with the hole for the spark plug down its axis. It goes in the secondary of a Thermonuclear Bomb (up to six) or of an Intercontinental Ballistic Missile (up to four). Burnt completely it would give 2.5 megatons; a good device burns half.
tooltip.kiloton.exchange_column.info:
Separates isotopes by chemical exchange, the two halves of the fusion fuel.
Lithium: the COLEX process (lithium amalgam against lithium hydroxide): eight lithium make one lithium-6, 600k FE.
Water: the Girdler sulfide process: a bucket of water makes one flask of heavy water and gives the bucket back, 1.8M FE.
Runs on Forge Energy like the other machines (coal in its slot, a Nuclear Cell, cables, a Breeder Reactor next to it). Hoppers and pipes work.
tooltip.kiloton.icbm.info:
A two-stage missile for a two-stage warhead. It goes on a Launch Pad, where it stands four blocks tall, and flies three times as far as the Ballistic Missile. With it on the pad the panel shows the warhead's second stage: up to four Lithium-6 Deuteride Charges, a spark plug and a uranium jacket, behind the usual pit and tamper (the primary). Full, about 10 megatons.
Radar, sirens and interceptor batteries treat it like any other missile.
tooltip.kiloton.long_range_detonator.inf: A Remote Detonator with a transmitter for megaton distances: 100 km instead of 10, far enough to set off a Thermonuclear Bomb from outside its reach (15 megatons break windows 57 km away). It works like the other one: sneak-use it on a bomb to link it, then use it anywhere in the same dimension and type the bomb's arming code.
block.kiloton.creative_source.status: Creative source: endless FE on every side
tooltip.kiloton.creative_source.info: Endless Forge Energy, pushed out on every side: as much as the machines and cables next to it will take. It cannot be crafted: it is for creative building, tests and videos.
tooltip.kiloton.exosuit_helmet.info:
Part of the exosuit, the level-2 suit: a sealed helmet with its own air and twin filters.
The suit protects only with all four pieces on and power left in the chestplate.
tooltip.kiloton.exosuit_chestplate.info:
The exosuit: armour plate over a sealed hazmat layer, its own air, a power unit on the back. Worn whole and charged it stops almost everything: the flash, fire, the blast wave, falls, the prompt radiation, fallout and contamination, and its air never runs out. Not the inside of a fireball.
Protecting uses the charge: a second for every second under fire, plus a share for each hit (half a second per point of damage, a minute at most). Full, it lasts 10 minutes; it recharges by itself in 20 once nothing is happening. The bar is the charge.
tooltip.kiloton.exosuit_leggings.info: Part of the exosuit, the level-2 suit. It protects only with all four pieces on and power left in the chestplate.
tooltip.kiloton.exosuit_boots.info:
Part of the exosuit, the level-2 suit. Heavy boots: the wind of a blast leans on the suit but cannot throw it.
It protects only with all four pieces on and power left in the chestplate.
tooltip.kiloton.atomic_glass.info: Sand the fireball melted into clear green glass, full of bubbles. It forms on sandy ground near ground zero, between the trinitite crust and plain glass. It breaks like glass: only silk touch keeps it. Faintly radioactive.
effect.kiloton.radiation_sickness.descri: Damage that does not heal by itself until the body repairs the dose.
block.kiloton.cable.status: %s: %s FE/t per connection · network of %s cables, %s FE stored, %s outlets
block.kiloton.cable.mode.normal: %s side: normal (gives power to what it touches)
block.kiloton.cable.mode.extract: %s side: extract (pulls power out of what it touches)
tooltip.kiloton.copper_cable.info: Carries Forge Energy: cables join by themselves to each other and to anything that stores, makes or uses power, Kiloton's and other mods'. Generators push into it and the network hands the power out to the machines. To pull power out of a battery or a machine that does not push, Shift-right-click with an empty hand on the cable's side next to it: normal, extract (amber plate), disconnected. Right-click shows the network. Copper: 1,000 FE/t per connection.
tooltip.kiloton.gold_cable.info: Like the copper cable, eight times faster: 8,000 FE/t per connection. Shift-right-click a side with an empty hand: normal, extract, disconnected. Grades join into one network; each connection moves what its own cable allows.
tooltip.kiloton.hardened_cable.info: Like the copper cable, diamond-hardened: 64,000 FE/t per connection, enough for a breeder reactor and a cascade of centrifuges. Shift-right-click a side with an empty hand: normal, extract, disconnected.
tooltip.kiloton.superconducting_cable.in: No resistance at all: 1,000,000 FE/t per connection, for the mods that make megawatts. Shift-right-click a side with an empty hand: normal, extract, disconnected.
kiloton.vault_door.no_room: No room for the vault door: it goes at the bottom middle of a free %1$sx%1$s opening, facing in, with a free strip one block deep along the inner wall, %2$s blocks wide on one side, to roll into
kiloton.vault_door.blocked: Something is in the way: the door needs the strip over its track clear to roll aside
tooltip.kiloton.blast_door.info: A steel door that opens by hand or by redstone, like a wooden one. Shut, it is a shelter wall that holds about 20 psi: it stops the flash, the fallout and the wind, but a close burst blows it in. A shelter is as strong as its weakest wall or door.
tooltip.kiloton.bunker_door.info: A thick steel bunker door with a handwheel: holds about 60 psi shut, as much as a heavy concrete shelter. Opens by hand or by redstone. A shelter is as strong as its weakest wall or door.
tooltip.kiloton.blast_hatch.info: A steel hatch for a shelter entered from above: holds about 60 psi shut. Opens by hand or by redstone.
tooltip.kiloton.vault_door.info: A round steel vault door, a gear on a toothed track: shut, it holds 2,000 psi, so only the crater itself is stronger. Place it at the bottom middle of a 3x3 opening, looking into the shelter. Inside it needs a free strip one block deep along the wall, 6 blocks wide on one side: it lays its track along the floor there, and opening, the handwheel unlocks it, the plate is pulled back onto the track and rolls aside along it. It does not open by hand: use a Vault Door Console within 16 blocks, a paired Vault Door Remote (from inside or outside, up to 64 blocks away), or give any part of it a redstone signal.
tooltip.kiloton.vault_door_console.info: Works the nearest vault door within 16 blocks, from inside the shelter or outside it: throw the lever to open it, throw it back to close it. The lever follows the door whoever moves it (another console, a remote, redstone).
kiloton.vault_door.use_console: A vault door does not open by hand: use its console, a paired remote or redstone
tooltip.kiloton.vault_door_remote.info: Opens and closes one vault door from up to 64 blocks away, from inside the shelter or from outside it. Sneak and use it on the door or on its console to pair it, then use it anywhere to send the door open or shut. Any number of remotes can be paired with the same door.
kiloton.vault_remote.paired: Remote paired with the vault door at %s %s %s
kiloton.vault_remote.unpaired: Not paired yet: sneak and use it on a vault door or its console
kiloton.vault_remote.other_dimension: The paired vault door is in another dimension
kiloton.vault_remote.out_of_range: No signal: the door is %s blocks away, the remote reaches %s
kiloton.vault_remote.gone: The paired vault door at %s %s %s is not there any more
tooltip.kiloton.large_vault_door.info: The vault door for a 5x5 opening: a heavier gear, 28 teeth, rolling 5 blocks aside on its own track. Shut, it holds 2,000 psi like the small one. Place it at the bottom middle of a 5x5 opening, looking into the shelter; inside it needs a free strip one block deep along the wall, 10 blocks wide on one side. It opens from a Vault Door Console within 16 blocks, a paired Vault Door Remote or a redstone signal on any part of it.
